Summary statistics of a metacommunity

Source: R/summary_stats.R
summary_stats.Rd

The same statistics for simulated and observed data, so that they can be compared or used for inference. Each statistic that lacks its inputs is NA, so the result always has the same names and results can be bound by rows.

Usage

summary_stats(
  x,
  tree = NULL,
  trait = NULL,
  env = NULL,
  coords = NULL,
  n_null = 99
)

Arguments

x

An mc_sim object, a matrix with one row per site and one column per species, or an array of sites x species x steps. In an array, the last step gives the statistics that are not temporal. From an mc_sim, these come from abundance and the temporal ones from history, and env, coords and trait default to those of the simulation, the trait being the environmental optimum.

tree

Optional phylo object, matched to species by name.

trait

Optional numeric vector with one value per species, named by species.

env

Optional numeric vector with one value per site.

coords

Optional matrix or data frame with one row per site and the coordinates in columns.

n_null

Number of shuffles of species for ses_mpd and ses_mntd.

Value

Named numeric vector.

Details

alpha, gamma and beta are the mean number of species per site, the number of species in all sites and gamma / alpha. occupancy and occupancy_sd are the mean and the standard deviation of the share of sites each species occupies, over the species present. abundance is the mean number of individuals per site, evenness the mean Pielou evenness of sites with two or more species, evenness_regional the same for all sites together and sad_sd the standard deviation of the logarithm of regional abundances, which describes the species abundance distribution. With 0/1 data, these last four describe frequencies of occurrence.

ses_mpd and ses_mntd need tree. They are the standardised effect sizes of the mean pairwise distance and of the mean nearest taxon distance, from presences, averaged over sites with two or more species. The null model shuffles species across the tips, as null.model = "taxa.labels" of picante::ses.mpd(), so the pool is all the species shared by x and tree, including those without individuals. Compare results only between data with the same pool. This is the only part that uses random numbers.

decay needs coords. It is the correlation between Bray-Curtis dissimilarity and distance among occupied sites. trait_env needs trait and env: the correlation between the mean trait of each site, weighted by abundance, and the environment. trait_sd is the standard deviation of the trait among all individuals.

The temporal statistics need at least two steps, from history or an array. cv_population, cv_site and cv_regional are mean coefficients of variation over time: of each species in each site, of the individuals of each site, and of each species in all sites, leaving out those that are always absent. turnover is the mean Bray-Curtis dissimilarity of a site between consecutive steps. Guzman et al. (2022) found that temporal statistics added explanatory power, and that dispersal depended on them.

References

Guzman, L. M., Thompson, P. L., Viana, D. S., Vanschoenwinkel, B., Horváth, Z., Ptacnik, R., Jeliazkov, A., Gascón, S., Lemmens, P., Anton-Pardo, M., Langenheder, S., De Meester, L., & Chase, J. M. (2022). Accounting for temporal change in multiple biodiversity patterns improves the inference of metacommunity processes. Ecology, 103, e3683. doi:10.1002/ecy.3683

Examples

set.seed(1)
tree <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(15)
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(landscape_grid(side = 5), species_traits(tree),
                              competition_matrix(tree, "phylo"), n_steps = 60,
                              seed_steps = 1:5, record_steps = seq(40, 60, by = 5))
round(summary_stats(sim, tree, n_null = 19), 3)
#>             alpha             gamma              beta         occupancy 
#>             5.720            13.000             2.273             0.440 
#>      occupancy_sd         abundance          evenness evenness_regional 
#>             0.334           239.720             0.766             0.841 
#>            sad_sd           ses_mpd          ses_mntd             decay 
#>             1.185             0.185            -0.251             0.163 
#>         trait_env          trait_sd     cv_population           cv_site 
#>             0.951            19.708             0.771             0.082 
#>       cv_regional          turnover 
#>             0.275             0.107
